method: A curated, expandable world-history archive. Events are selected examples rather than an exhaustive record of every event; dates and interpretations may be debated. Entries link to educational, institutional or reference sources.

events.title: Agriculture begins to transform human societies
events.summary: In several regions, people increasingly cultivated plants and managed animals. These changes supported settled communities, food surpluses and eventually larger societies.

events.title: Sumerian cities grow in Mesopotamia
events.summary: Urban centres such as Uruk expanded in southern Mesopotamia, supported by irrigation, specialised labour, trade and increasingly complex administration.

events.title: Writing develops in Mesopotamia
events.summary: Early cuneiform records helped communities track goods, labour and administration. Writing later became a tool for literature, law and historical memory.

events.title: Political unification of ancient Egypt
events.summary: The unification of Upper and Lower Egypt is traditionally associated with the beginning of the first dynastic period and a long tradition of pharaonic rule.

events.title: Indus Valley cities flourish
events.summary: Harappa and Mohenjo-daro became major urban centres, known for planned streets, drainage systems, craft production and long-distance trade.

events.title: Great Pyramid of Giza is built
events.summary: The pyramid built for Pharaoh Khufu became the largest monument of the Giza pyramid complex and one of the most enduring achievements of ancient engineering.

events.title: Akkadian Empire unites much of Mesopotamia
events.summary: Sargon of Akkad built an empire linking cities across Mesopotamia, creating one of the earliest known territorial states.

events.title: Hammurabi's law code is issued
events.summary: The Babylonian king Hammurabi's law collection records rules and penalties covering social, economic and family life in his kingdom.

events.title: Shang dynasty rules in northern China
events.summary: The Shang period is associated with early Chinese writing on oracle bones, bronze craftsmanship and the growth of organised states.

events.title: New Kingdom Egypt begins
events.summary: Egypt entered a period of imperial expansion, monumental building and wide diplomatic and commercial connections.

events.title: Late Bronze Age systems collapse across the eastern Mediterranean
events.summary: Several major palace societies and trade networks experienced disruption. The causes differed by region and remain a subject of historical debate.

events.title: Olmec centres flourish in Mesoamerica
events.summary: Olmec communities developed influential ceremonial centres, art styles and cultural traditions in parts of present-day Mexico.

events.title: Kingdom of Kush emerges as a major power
events.summary: Nubian kingdoms developed south of Egypt and later ruled Egypt during the Twenty-fifth Dynasty.

events.title: Zhou dynasty replaces Shang rule in China
events.summary: The Zhou established a long-lasting political order and developed ideas about legitimate rule, including the Mandate of Heaven.

events.title: First recorded ancient Olympic Games
events.summary: The earliest recorded Olympic festival took place at Olympia in Greece. Athletic contests later became a major shared institution of the Greek world.

events.title: Confucius teaches in China
events.summary: Confucius' teachings on ethics, learning, social relationships and responsible government became foundational to later Chinese intellectual and political traditions.

events.title: Achaemenid Persian Empire is founded
events.summary: Cyrus the Great established an empire that connected a vast territory from western Asia to parts of Central Asia and the eastern Mediterranean.

events.title: Roman Republic begins
events.summary: According to Roman tradition, the monarchy was replaced by a republic. Roman institutions and expansion would shape the Mediterranean world for centuries.

events.title: Athenian democratic reforms
events.summary: Reforms associated with Cleisthenes reorganised political participation among male citizens in Athens, becoming an influential early experiment in democracy.

events.title: Maya civilisation develops across Mesoamerica
events.summary: Maya cities and communities built sophisticated systems of writing, mathematics, astronomy and monumental architecture over many centuries.

events.title: Buddha's teachings take shape in South Asia
events.summary: The teachings associated with Siddhartha Gautama emerged in the religious and philosophical world of ancient northern India and later spread across Asia.

events.title: Alexander's campaigns reshape the eastern Mediterranean
events.summary: Macedonian conquest spread Greek political and cultural influence across Egypt and parts of western and central Asia.

events.title: Mauryan Empire rises in India
events.summary: Chandragupta Maurya established an empire across much of the Indian subcontinent, creating one of ancient South Asia's largest states.

events.title: Ashoka promotes Buddhist teachings
events.summary: After the Kalinga war, Mauryan emperor Ashoka supported policies associated with dhamma and helped Buddhism gain wider influence across South Asia.

events.title: Qin unifies China
events.summary: Qin Shi Huang conquered rival states and established the first unified imperial dynasty, standardising important systems of administration, writing and measurement.

events.title: Roman Empire begins
events.summary: Octavian became Augustus, marking the transition from the Roman Republic to imperial rule and a new political order around the Mediterranean.

events.title: Teotihuacan grows into a major Mesoamerican city
events.summary: Teotihuacan became one of the largest urban centres in the ancient Americas, with far-reaching cultural influence.

events.title: Christianity emerges in the Roman world
events.summary: The movement formed around the life and teachings of Jesus spread through communities in the eastern Mediterranean and eventually across the Roman Empire.

events.title: Silk Roads connect Eurasian regions
events.summary: A network of land and sea routes moved goods, technologies, religions and ideas between East Asia, Central Asia, South Asia, the Middle East and Europe.

events.title: Aksum becomes a major Red Sea trading power
events.summary: The kingdom of Aksum connected northeast Africa with Arabia and the wider Indian Ocean trade network.

events.title: Gupta Empire rises in northern India
events.summary: The Gupta rulers established a major North Indian empire associated with developments in mathematics, literature, art and political culture.

events.title: Classic Maya cities reach a period of major influence
events.summary: Maya city-states flourished through regional trade, monumental construction and advances in calendrical and written knowledge.

events.title: Western Roman imperial rule ends
events.summary: The deposition of the last western Roman emperor is conventionally used as a marker for the end of the Western Roman Empire, though Roman institutions continued in the east.

events.title: Muhammad's first revelations begin in Islam's tradition
events.summary: The beginnings of Islam are traditionally dated to the early seventh century in western Arabia, where a new religious community took shape.

events.title: Tang dynasty begins in China
events.summary: The Tang era became a major period of Chinese imperial power, urban culture, international exchange and literary achievement.

events.title: Tang China enters a period of expansion and cultural influence
events.summary: The Tang dynasty presided over major developments in government, trade, literature and urban culture across East Asia.

events.title: Hijra marks the beginning of the Islamic calendar
events.summary: Muhammad and his followers migrated from Mecca to Medina. The migration became a turning point in the formation of the early Muslim community.

events.title: Umayyad forces enter the Iberian Peninsula
events.summary: The conquest initiated centuries of changing Muslim and Christian rule, exchange and conflict in parts of Iberia.

events.title: Gopala establishes the Pala dynasty
events.summary: Gopala emerged as ruler in a period of political fragmentation and founded a dynasty that would shape Bengal for roughly four centuries. The exact dates of early Pala reigns remain approximate.

events.title: Abbasid Caliphate becomes a major centre of scholarship
events.summary: The Abbasid era supported important intellectual networks in cities including Baghdad, where scholars translated, debated and developed works in mathematics, medicine, astronomy and philosophy.

events.title: Dharmapala expands Pala influence
events.summary: Under Dharmapala, the Palas became a major power in northern India. His reign is also associated with major Buddhist institutions, including the foundation of Somapura Mahavihara at Paharpur.

events.title: Somapura Mahavihara flourishes
events.summary: Built under Pala patronage, the great monastery at Paharpur became a renowned intellectual centre and an influential example of Buddhist architecture in South Asia.

events.title: Ghana and later West African empires flourish
events.summary: Trans-Saharan trade helped support powerful states in West Africa, linking gold-producing regions with North African and wider commercial networks.

events.title: Charlemagne is crowned emperor
events.summary: The coronation strengthened a new western European imperial ideal and shaped political and religious institutions in medieval Europe.

events.title: Khmer Empire is established
events.summary: The political formation associated with Jayavarman II laid foundations for the Khmer Empire, whose rulers built the Angkor complex in present-day Cambodia.

events.title: Song dynasty reunifies much of China
events.summary: The Song period saw major developments in commerce, printing, urban life, technology and state administration.

events.title: Song dynasty begins in China
events.summary: The Song era saw major growth in commerce, cities, printing, technology and state administration.

events.title: Polynesian voyaging expands across the Pacific
events.summary: Skilled navigators settled and connected islands across vast stretches of the Pacific, carrying crops, knowledge and cultural traditions.

events.title: First Crusade begins
events.summary: A western European military expedition set out for the eastern Mediterranean, beginning a series of crusading campaigns with lasting effects across the region.

events.title: Sena power rises in Bengal
events.summary: The Sena dynasty rose in the second half of the 12th century, bringing Pala rule in Bengal to an end. Chronologies for this transition vary across historical accounts.

events.title: Great Zimbabwe develops as a major southern African centre
events.summary: The stone-built settlement became an important political and trading centre connected to Indian Ocean commerce.

events.title: Turkish conquest reshapes Bengal's political order
events.summary: The campaigns associated with Muhammad Bakhtiyar Khalji marked the beginning of a new phase of Muslim political rule in parts of Bengal. Control consolidated unevenly across the region.

events.title: Mongol Empire is proclaimed
events.summary: Temujin was recognised as Chinggis Khan, beginning the expansion of a steppe empire that would connect large parts of Eurasia through conquest and exchange.

events.title: Magna Carta is sealed in England
events.summary: King John agreed to a charter that placed certain limits on royal authority. Its later interpretations influenced constitutional and legal traditions.

events.title: Mali Empire rises in West Africa
events.summary: The state associated with Sundiata Keita grew into a major power controlling important gold and trade routes across the western Sahel.

events.title: Mongol forces capture Baghdad
events.summary: The conquest ended the Abbasid caliphate's political authority in Baghdad and transformed the region's intellectual and political landscape.

events.title: Mongol conquest completes the Song-Yuan transition in China
events.summary: The Yuan dynasty consolidated Mongol rule over China, connecting it to a wider Eurasian imperial network.

events.title: Mansa Musa's pilgrimage highlights Mali's wealth
events.summary: The ruler of Mali travelled to Mecca, drawing attention to the empire's gold wealth and trans-Saharan connections.

events.title: An independent Bengal Sultanate takes shape
events.summary: Shamsuddin Ilyas Shah consolidated an independent sultanate centred on Lakhnauti, helping establish a more unified political identity for Bengal.

events.title: Black Death devastates parts of Afro-Eurasia
events.summary: The plague spread through trade and travel networks, causing catastrophic mortality and profound economic and social change across many regions.

events.title: Inca state expands in the Andes
events.summary: The Inca built an extensive Andean state supported by roads, administration, agriculture and regional integration.

events.title: Inca imperial expansion accelerates
events.summary: Under Pachacuti and his successors, the Inca state expanded across the Andes and developed an extensive road and administrative network.

events.title: Movable-type printing transforms European book production
events.summary: Johannes Gutenberg's printing innovations helped make books and printed texts easier to reproduce in Europe, accelerating the circulation of ideas.

events.title: Ottoman conquest of Constantinople
events.summary: The city fell to Ottoman forces under Mehmed II, ending the Byzantine Empire and establishing a new centre of Ottoman power.

events.title: Columbus reaches the Caribbean
events.summary: The voyage initiated sustained contact between Europe and the Americas, followed by conquest, colonisation, forced migration and major biological and economic exchanges.

events.title: Protestant Reformation begins
events.summary: Martin Luther's challenge to church practices helped trigger religious and political changes across Europe, reshaping Christianity and state power.

events.title: Mughal Empire is founded in India
events.summary: Babur's victory at Panipat established Mughal rule in northern India, beginning an empire that would profoundly influence South Asian politics, architecture and culture.

events.title: Bengal is incorporated into the Mughal Empire
events.summary: Mughal authority expanded across Bengal after the campaigns of Akbar's reign. Local resistance and regional power centres continued to shape the process of consolidation.
events.source: Bangladesh: A Country Study · Federal Research Division

events.title: Scientific Revolution reshapes European inquiry
events.summary: New methods of observation, experiment and mathematical reasoning transformed the study of nature, with developments taking place across a wider global history of knowledge.

events.title: Tokugawa rule begins in Japan
events.summary: The Tokugawa shogunate established a political order that shaped Japan for more than two and a half centuries.

events.title: Dutch East India Company is founded
events.summary: The VOC became a powerful chartered trading company, illustrating the growing role of corporate and state-backed maritime empires in global commerce.

events.title: Dhaka becomes a Mughal provincial capital
events.summary: Dhaka, known as Jahangirnagar during the Mughal period, became an important administrative and commercial centre in Bengal. The exact year of the capital's transfer is described differently in historical accounts.
events.source: Bangladesh: A Country Study · Federal Research Division

events.title: Peace of Westphalia reshapes European diplomacy
events.summary: The treaties ending the Thirty Years' War helped establish new patterns of diplomacy and territorial sovereignty in Europe.

events.title: Newton publishes Principia
events.summary: Isaac Newton's work set out influential laws of motion and universal gravitation, becoming a landmark in the history of physics and mathematical science.

events.title: Battle of Plassey
events.summary: The East India Company defeated Nawab Siraj ud-Daulah after the defection of key commanders, including Mir Jafar. The outcome opened the way for Company political dominance in Bengal.

events.title: Industrial Revolution transforms production
events.summary: Mechanisation, new energy systems, factories and transport reshaped economies and societies, first in Britain and then across many parts of the world.

events.title: The East India Company obtains the Diwani
events.summary: The Company secured the right to collect revenue in Bengal, Bihar and Orissa, deepening its control over the region's finances and administration.
events.source: Bangladesh: A Country Study · Federal Research Division

events.title: American Declaration of Independence
events.summary: Thirteen British colonies declared themselves independent, launching a revolutionary conflict that led to the creation of the United States.

events.title: French Revolution begins
events.summary: The revolution challenged the monarchy and old social order in France, spreading new debates about citizenship, rights, sovereignty and political authority.

events.title: Haitian Revolution creates an independent state
events.summary: Enslaved and free people of colour fought French colonial rule. Haiti became independent in 1804, making the revolution a landmark in the history of slavery and emancipation.

events.title: Permanent Settlement introduced
events.summary: The colonial government fixed land revenue demands and recognised zamindars as revenue-collecting landholders. Its effects on cultivators and agrarian relations remained deeply contested.

events.title: Haitian independence is declared
events.summary: After a revolution against slavery and French colonial rule, Haiti became an independent state and a landmark in the history of emancipation.

events.title: Britain abolishes its transatlantic slave trade
events.summary: The British Parliament outlawed the British slave trade, though slavery itself continued in the empire until later abolition and the wider Atlantic system persisted elsewhere.
events.source: UK Parliament · Slavery and the British Parliament

events.title: Independence movements transform Latin America
events.summary: A wave of independence campaigns dismantled much of Spain's colonial rule in the Americas and created new states.

events.title: Indian Rebellion challenges East India Company rule
events.summary: A major uprising involving soldiers, rulers and civilians challenged Company authority. Its suppression led to the transfer of governance to the British Crown in 1858.

events.title: American Civil War begins
events.summary: The conflict over secession and slavery became a defining struggle over the future of the United States.

events.title: Meiji Restoration transforms Japan
events.summary: Political change restored imperial rule and initiated rapid state-led reforms in administration, industry, education and the military.

events.title: Berlin Conference formalises rules for European claims in Africa
events.summary: European powers negotiated rules for colonial claims during the Scramble for Africa without African representation, accelerating imperial partition and occupation.

events.title: Partition of Bengal takes effect
events.summary: The province was divided and a new province of Eastern Bengal and Assam was created. The decision triggered powerful, diverse political responses, including Swadeshi mobilisation and support for the new province among sections of the population.

events.title: Swadeshi and boycott movements spread
events.summary: Opposition to the partition helped popularise the use of locally made goods, boycotts of imported British products, public meetings and new forms of political organisation. Participation and opinion differed across communities and regions.

events.title: Partition of Bengal is annulled
events.summary: The British government reversed the 1905 arrangement amid sustained political agitation. The reorganisation also changed the administrative map of eastern India.

events.title: First World War begins
events.summary: The assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand triggered a crisis that escalated into a global war involving European empires and societies across several continents.

events.title: Russian Revolution brings Bolsheviks to power
events.summary: Revolutionary upheaval ended the Russian monarchy and later brought the Bolsheviks to power, leading to the creation of the Soviet state.

events.title: Armistice ends the fighting in the First World War
events.summary: The armistice of 11 November halted fighting on the Western Front. Peace settlements and political upheavals continued to reshape the post-war world.

events.title: Treaty of Versailles is signed
events.summary: The peace settlement formally ended the state of war between Germany and the Allied powers and reshaped post-war Europe.
events.source: Council on Foreign Relations · Essential Events

events.title: University of Dhaka opens
events.summary: The university began with three faculties, twelve departments, sixty teachers, 877 students and three residential halls, becoming a major centre of higher education in the region.

events.title: Great Depression begins
events.summary: A financial collapse in the United States developed into a worldwide economic crisis, bringing mass unemployment, social hardship and political instability.

events.title: Second World War begins in Europe
events.summary: Germany's invasion of Poland led Britain and France to declare war. The conflict expanded into a global war that caused unprecedented destruction and genocide.

events.title: Bengal Famine
events.summary: Wartime disruption, inflation, failures in food distribution and policy decisions contributed to a catastrophic famine. Estimates of mortality vary; the event devastated households and livelihoods across Bengal.

events.title: United Nations is founded
events.summary: Representatives of 50 countries signed the UN Charter in San Francisco in June 1945. The organisation formally came into existence in October.
events.source: United Nations · History of the UN

events.title: Second World War ends
events.summary: The war ended in Europe in May and in the Pacific in September 1945, after the defeat of the Axis powers and the atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki.

events.title: Partition of British India
events.summary: British India was divided into India and Pakistan. East Bengal became Pakistan's eastern wing, separated geographically from West Pakistan by Indian territory.
events.source: Bangladesh: A Country Study · Federal Research Division

events.title: Universal Declaration of Human Rights is adopted
events.summary: The UN General Assembly adopted the declaration, setting out a common statement of fundamental rights and freedoms.
events.source: United Nations · Universal Declaration of Human Rights

events.title: State of Israel is established and the Nakba unfolds
events.summary: The end of the British Mandate and the declaration of Israel were accompanied by the mass displacement of Palestinians, remembered as the Nakba.
events.source: Council on Foreign Relations · Essential Events

events.title: People's Republic of China is proclaimed
events.summary: The Chinese Communist Party established the People's Republic after the Chinese Civil War, transforming the political landscape of East Asia.

events.title: Korean War begins
events.summary: War on the Korean peninsula drew in international forces and entrenched the division between North and South Korea.
events.source: Council on Foreign Relations · Essential Events

events.title: Language Movement reaches a turning point
events.summary: Police fired on demonstrators in Dhaka during protests demanding recognition of Bangla. The movement continued, and Bangla became one of Pakistan's state languages in 1956.

events.title: Bandung Conference brings Asian and African states together
events.summary: Delegates from 29 countries met in Indonesia to discuss anti-colonialism, sovereignty, economic cooperation and international relations during the Cold War.

events.title: Bangla gains state-language recognition in Pakistan
events.summary: The Pakistan Constituent Assembly adopted Bangla and Urdu as state languages, following years of public mobilisation and political pressure.

events.title: Ghana becomes independent
events.summary: Ghana's independence became a landmark in African decolonisation and inspired liberation movements across the continent.

events.title: A wave of African independence accelerates
events.summary: Seventeen African countries became independent in 1960, marking a major moment in the wider process of decolonisation across the continent.

events.title: African Union predecessor, the OAU, is founded
events.summary: Independent African states established the Organisation of African Unity to promote solidarity and support decolonisation.

events.title: US Civil Rights Act is signed
events.summary: The legislation prohibited segregation in public places and discrimination in employment, marking a major victory in the US civil rights movement.
events.source: Council on Foreign Relations · Essential Events

events.title: Six-Point Programme presented
events.summary: Sheikh Mujibur Rahman presented a programme demanding far-reaching autonomy for East Pakistan, covering federal government, currency, taxation, trade and security arrangements.

events.title: Mass uprising forces a political turning point
events.summary: A broad student-led and popular movement challenged the Ayub regime. Sheikh Mujibur Rahman was released on 22 February, and the title Bangabandhu was conferred on him the following day.

events.title: Apollo 11 lands the first humans on the Moon
events.summary: Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin walked on the lunar surface while Michael Collins remained in lunar orbit, marking a defining moment in space exploration.

events.title: Pakistan's general election
events.summary: The Awami League won an overwhelming majority of the seats allocated to East Pakistan, giving it a clear electoral mandate. The transfer of power did not take place as expected.

events.title: Historic 7 March speech
events.summary: At the Ramna Racecourse in Dhaka, Sheikh Mujibur Rahman delivered an address that became a defining moment in the struggle for self-determination. UNESCO later inscribed the speech in its Memory of the World Register.

events.title: Bangladesh's independence struggle begins
events.summary: Following the Pakistan army's crackdown, the declaration of independence and armed resistance marked the beginning of the Bangladesh Liberation War.

events.title: Victory in the Liberation War
events.summary: Pakistani forces surrendered in Dhaka, ending the nine-month war and establishing Bangladesh as an independent state.

events.title: Vietnam War ends
events.summary: The fall of Saigon ended the war and led to the reunification of Vietnam under the communist government.
events.source: Council on Foreign Relations · Essential Events

events.title: Iranian Revolution transforms the state
events.summary: The revolution overthrew the Pahlavi monarchy and established the Islamic Republic, reshaping politics in the Middle East.
events.source: Council on Foreign Relations · Essential Events

events.title: Berlin Wall opens
events.summary: The opening of the Berlin Wall followed months of public protest and political change in Eastern Europe, becoming a symbol of the end of the Cold War division of Europe.

events.title: Tiananmen Square protests are suppressed
events.summary: Pro-democracy demonstrations in Beijing were violently suppressed, becoming a major event in modern Chinese history.
events.source: Council on Foreign Relations · Essential Events

events.title: Soviet Union dissolves
events.summary: The Soviet Union ceased to exist in December, ending a major state structure of the twentieth century and reshaping international politics.

events.title: South Africa holds its first democratic multiracial election
events.summary: The election brought an end to apartheid rule and led to Nelson Mandela becoming president, marking a decisive transition in South African history.

events.title: Rwandan genocide
events.summary: The genocide against the Tutsi and the killing of moderate Hutu in Rwanda caused immense loss of life and lasting regional consequences.

events.title: September 11 attacks reshape global politics
events.summary: Coordinated terrorist attacks in the United States killed thousands and led to major changes in security policy and international military intervention.

events.title: Global financial crisis spreads
events.summary: The collapse of major financial institutions and credit markets triggered a worldwide recession and renewed debate about financial regulation and economic risk.

events.title: Arab Spring uprisings spread across the Middle East and North Africa
events.summary: Public protests challenged long-standing governments and triggered political upheaval and conflict across several countries.
events.source: Council on Foreign Relations · Essential Events

events.title: COVID-19 becomes a global pandemic
events.summary: The World Health Organization characterised COVID-19 as a pandemic in March 2020. The crisis disrupted health systems, travel, education and economies worldwide.
events.source: WHO · Timeline of WHO's COVID-19 response

events.title: Russia launches full-scale invasion of Ukraine
events.summary: The invasion escalated the war in Ukraine and triggered major humanitarian, security and diplomatic consequences across Europe and beyond.

people.name: Gopala
people.bio: Gopala emerged as ruler amid political disorder in Bengal and founded the Pala dynasty, which became one of the region's longest-lasting ruling houses.

people.name: Dharmapala
people.bio: A major Pala ruler whose reign expanded the dynasty's influence in northern India. Pala patronage supported important Buddhist institutions, including Somapura Mahavihara.

people.name: Shamsuddin Ilyas Shah
people.role: Founder of the Ilyas Shahi dynasty
people.bio: He consolidated an independent Bengal Sultanate and helped establish a political framework that brought several parts of Bengal under one ruler.

people.name: Siraj ud-Daulah
people.bio: The Nawab who faced the East India Company at Plassey in June 1757. His defeat, amid defections within his command, became a turning point in the Company's rise to power in Bengal.

people.name: Begum Rokeya
people.bio: Rokeya advocated women's education and social equality. Her writing, including the 1905 satire Sultana's Dream, challenged restrictions placed on women.

people.name: Rabindranath Tagore
people.bio: A central figure in Bengali literature, Tagore reshaped poetry, songs, fiction and educational thought. He received the 1913 Nobel Prize in Literature.

people.name: Jagadish Chandra Bose
people.bio: Bose conducted pioneering research in radio and microwave science and later developed sensitive instruments to study plant responses. He founded the Bose Institute in 1917.

people.name: Satyendra Nath Bose
people.bio: While teaching at the University of Dhaka, Bose developed the work on quantum statistics that he sent to Albert Einstein in 1924. The resulting framework became known as Bose–Einstein statistics.

people.name: A. K. Fazlul Huq
people.bio: A prominent Bengali political leader who served as Prime Minister of Bengal from 1937 to 1943. His career crossed provincial politics, agrarian questions and the politics of late colonial India.

people.name: Sheikh Mujibur Rahman
people.role: Political leader of the independence movement
people.bio: A central organiser of the autonomy movement in East Pakistan, he presented the Six-Point Programme in 1966 and led the Awami League to victory in the 1970 election. He became the first president of independent Bangladesh.

people.name: Dhirendranath Datta
people.bio: In February 1948, Datta moved an amendment in Pakistan's Constituent Assembly arguing that Bangla should be accepted as a language of the Assembly, an early parliamentary intervention in the language question.

people.name: Abul Kashem
people.bio: A professor and organiser associated with Tamaddun Majlish, he helped mobilise early advocacy for Bangla as a state language after the creation of Pakistan.
